newsitem.title: ESTONIA: ESTONIA - TALLINN TO BORROW 240 MLN KROONS IN 1998.
newsitem.headline: ESTONIA - TALLINN TO BORROW 240 MLN KROONS IN 1998.

text.p: The Tallinn City government said on Friday it proposed to city council to issue bonds or take a loan of 240 million kroons in 1998.

"We need to take a loan to guarantee the stability in investments, otherwise the investment level will fall from the present level of 300 million kroons to 120 million kroons," Ants Leemets, deputy mayor, told Reuters.
The city government on Friday approved the 1998 budget principles, which also include the imposition of a sales tax of one percent from July 1, 1998.
"The alternative would be the establishment of a tourism tax," Leemets told a news conference.
Leemets said the loan sum was optimal.
"We can not take more, otherwise the liablities will be too large," he added.
Leemets also said Tallinn plans to take the loan or issue bonds by tapping the international capital markets.
"The banks are ready to give the credit," he added.
Tallinn last year issued bonds worth 480 million kroons through Nomura. Leemets said the city's debt is 220 million kroons this year.
It paid Nomura 110 million kroons this year and another loan payment is due in October.
